commands.summary: 6/6 bridge tests passed: end-to-end margin soundness, direct head difference vs separate logits, strict positive acceptance & tie rejection, profile binding, real near-tie witness & confident sample verification, and artifact generation

requirement_evidence.evidence: FLOAT32_BRIDGE.md §1 derives the complete composition of raw conversion, normalization, 3 Conv layers, 3 BN layers, 3 ReLU layers, 2 MaxPool layers, Flatten, and 2 Linear layers. Proves that lower_margin_j = round_down_f32(lo_c - hi_j) strictly lower-bounds the executable logit difference fl(z_c) - fl(z_j). Verified by test_c01_end_to_end_margin_bounds_soundness.

FLOAT32_BRIDGE.md §2 and compute_margin_bounds support both 'separate_logits' and 'direct_head_difference'. For direct head difference, the lower bound is explicitly widened by the sum of backward rounding errors of both separate reference dot products (delta_c + delta_j), preserving conservatism over two rounded PyTorch logits. Verified by test_c02_direct_head_difference_accounts_for_rounding_errors.

Safe margin acceptance predicate is strictly positive (min_{j != c*} lower_margin_j > 0.0). Ties (margin == 0.0) and negative margins strictly return is_positive = False. Non-finite values fail closed. Verified by test_c03_safe_margin_predicate_rejects_ties_and_negatives.

Proof is cryptographically bound to profile linux-x86_64-py311-numpy246-torch2141cpu-avx512, SmallCNN1D checkpoint SHA-256, preprocessing ID, and dot lengths in {30, 96, 128, 192, 2048}. Unsupported profile fails closed. Verified by test_c04_profile_mismatch_fails_closed.

Near-tie control evaluated on real test sample row 13358 (executable margin 1.13487e-4): because margin is smaller than multi-layer accumulated Higham bound (~0.03), verifier soundly rejects certification (is_positive = False, status = VALIDATED_INCONCLUSIVE), preventing false positives. On confident sample row 15031 (margin 2.23), bridge proves VALIDATED_POSITIVE. Verified by test_c05_real_dataset_near_tie_witness.

FLOAT32_BRIDGE.md §5 and numerical_bridge.json provide end-to-end derivation and explain why interval wrapping across 15 layers causes margin collapse for perturbation radii epsilon >= 1e-4, formalizing the theoretical limitation of regional IBP certification on continuous streams without arbitrary safety factors.
Recorded cost and tightness diagnostics in bridge_checks.json and numerical_bridge.json, preparing full evidence base for independent review in W4-010. Verified by test_c06_c07_artifact_generation.

protected_hash_check: PASSED (214/214 files clean) via scripts/week4_audit.py check
scientific_dispositions: Confirms H05/H06/H08: An end-to-end mathematically sound float32 bridge exists for SmallCNN1D(num_classes=12) under backward rounding error bounds. The safe margin predicate is strictly positive and conservative.

Proves the near-tie boundary mechanism: inputs with executable margins smaller than accumulated rounding slack are soundly classified as VALIDATED_INCONCLUSIVE, precluding unsound certificate issuance.
limitations: End-to-end bridge provides point-wise and small-radius float32 guarantees; for regional boxes with epsilon >= 1e-4, multi-layer interval wrapping causes margin collapse (min_lower_margin < 0).
